rules.confirmed_detection_limitations: Same agent and source IP do not prove account compromise or matching usernames: failures use data.srcuser and successes data.dstuser. An unrelated success from another IP cannot complete the sequence.
rules.fixture_defects_and_recoveries: No additional discrepancy identified by scalar predicate/join/time audit
rules.objective: Detects an SSH brute-force alert followed by successful authentication on the same Wazuh agent within 15 minutes.
rules.production_dependencies: Collect SSH brute-force and successful authentication alerts with populated native source IP and agent join fields.

rules.confirmed_detection_limitations: SSH and sudo users are not equated. Substring matching can miss shells and alternative commands. This contextual rule overlaps PRIV-001 and PERS-001; prefer their additional evidence. Routine administration can match.
rules.fixture_defects_and_recoveries: No additional discrepancy identified by scalar predicate/join/time audit
rules.objective: Detects successful SSH authentication followed by privileged command execution within 15 minutes.
rules.production_dependencies: Collect SSH and sudo alerts with native command and target-user fields; review sensitive-command coverage.

rules.confirmed_detection_limitations: Realtime FIM reduces timing ambiguity but does not identify a process or SSH session. Scheduled-only monitoring is excluded and must remain covered by separate FIM alerts.
rules.fixture_defects_and_recoveries: No additional discrepancy identified by scalar predicate/join/time audit
rules.objective: Correlates remote access with subsequent modification of sensitive Linux authentication or access-control files. This SSH-linked rule is restricted to realtime FIM events
rules.production_dependencies: Enable realtime FIM for the specified authentication, sudoers and authorised-key paths.

rules.confirmed_detection_limitations: Agent and time correlation does not prove actor or session continuity. Unlike SSH-003 this source has no realtime FIM predicate; scheduled observation timing can misattribute changes. Legitimate administration can match.
rules.fixture_defects_and_recoveries: No additional discrepancy identified by scalar predicate/join/time audit
rules.objective: Detects a three-stage sequence involving remote access, privilege use and modification of security-sensitive files.
rules.production_dependencies: Collect SSH, sudo and sensitive-path FIM alerts; assess scheduled FIM observation delays.

rules.confirmed_detection_limitations: SCP command telemetry and FIM are joined only by agent and time; no transferred-file, user or session equality is enforced. Scheduled FIM and legitimate transfers can match.
rules.fixture_defects_and_recoveries: No additional discrepancy identified by scalar predicate/join/time audit
rules.objective: Detects an SSH login followed by SCP execution and a file creation or modification event.
rules.production_dependencies: Collect rule 92603 audit command telemetry identifying scp, SSH authentication and file FIM alerts.

rules.confirmed_detection_limitations: Same recorded client IP does not confirm exploitation. Historical attribution is uncertain because the recorded client address also represented the server public address; reverse proxies can link unrelated activity.
rules.fixture_defects_and_recoveries: No additional discrepancy identified by scalar predicate/join/time audit
rules.objective: This rule correlates reconnaissance and exploitation indicators originating from the same recorded HTTP client IP against the same Wazuh-monitored endpoint.
rules.production_dependencies: Collect HTTP reconnaissance and exploitation alerts; validate recorded client IP attribution through proxies.

rules.confirmed_detection_limitations: PHP creation is joined by endpoint and time, not HTTP client identity; causality is unproven. Legitimate deployments can create PHP files.
rules.fixture_defects_and_recoveries: No additional discrepancy identified by scalar predicate/join/time audit
rules.objective: This rule detects web attack indicators followed by the creation of a PHP file in the WordPress uploads directory.
rules.production_dependencies: Collect web alerts and added-file FIM in the exact WordPress Docker volume path; verify that path locally.

rules.confirmed_detection_limitations: Investigative correlation only: HTTP 200 does not prove exploitation. FIM detection time may differ from creation time, and legitimate deployments may match.
rules.fixture_defects_and_recoveries: No additional discrepancy identified by scalar predicate/join/time audit
rules.objective: This rule uses a narrower selection of web exploitation indicators followed by PHP file creation.
rules.production_dependencies: Collect the narrower exploitation rule IDs and added-file FIM at the exact WordPress Docker volume path.

rules.confirmed_detection_limitations: The requested PHP URL is not verified against the exact created file. Nested upload paths are included; the request stage deliberately has no rule-ID restriction, allowing other classifications including 31101.
rules.fixture_defects_and_recoveries: 46 original reversed fixtures; 16 FAIL retained; 51 separately recovered executions
rules.objective: This is the revised version. Instead of accepting general suspicious web activity after PHP creation, it requires a subsequent HTTP request targeting a PHP URL within the WordPress uploads directory.
rules.production_dependencies: Collect added-file FIM at the exact WordPress Docker volume path and native URL telemetry for uploads requests.

rules.confirmed_detection_limitations: The source says the optional third-stage key accommodates missing data.srcuser and that account creation remains associated by agent and time. Optional-field syntax does not itself guarantee wildcard joining: missing values can become null and fail to join a non-null username. Verify this claim in the target engine; do not silently change the query. SSH-to-sudo attribution is stronger, but account creation causality remains unproven. sudo su followed by useradd in a root shell is intentionally excluded.
rules.exact_query_evidence: 6A has response + rule byte hashes + parameters and preserved harness; no per-scenario serialized request. Compatibility supported by provenance, with this capture limitation.
rules.fixture_defects_and_recoveries: No new discrepancy identified by scalar predicate/join/time audit; MAL exclusion isolation and PRIV optional user remain limited.
rules.objective: Detects a successful SSH login followed by sudo activity targeting root and a subsequent new-user event on the same monitored endpoint.
rules.production_dependencies: Collect SSH destination usernames, sudo source usernames and commands, and 5902 new-user events. Validate stage-specific joins and missing third-stage usernames explicitly.

rules.production_dependencies: Collect SSH, 2834 crontab-editor alerts and FIM for all specified cron paths.
